messages:
ashley: Quick heads-up — running the biweekly admin sweep and I bumped into a weird KMS binding in project-prod. looks like a key has a cross-account IAM member: `serviceAccount:external-ci@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. anyone seen this before? :thinking:

samuel: saw a noisy alert from the kms-log-forwarder at 08:12 UTC. logs show `SetIamPolicy` change around 2026-03-20T08:10. payload snippet: `{"bindings":[{"role":"roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter","members":["serviceAccount:external-ci@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]}]}`

liam: ouch. that member shouldn't be in prod. can we confirm whether any running jobs still reference that key? I can grep deployments.

ashley: I pulled a list: `gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=redwood-prod --format=json` -> the key id is projects/???/locations/global/keyRings/redwood-prod/cryptoKeys/evt-ingest-key. Also `logs` show encryption calls from 10 different IPs over last 24h.

rachel: product impact: EVT pipeline and metrics ingestion talk to that key. if we rotate/disable we risk ~1-2min spikes and a retry backlog. acceptable if we coordinate with ops.

ashley: proposed playbook: 1) mark key disabled (prevent new encrypts), 2) create temp key & update non-prod consumers, 3) rotate production consumers to new key with canary, 4) remove cross-account binding, 5) re-enable or retire old key.

liam: small tweak: do step 0 -> snapshot IAM policy + export logs to a retention bucket (for audit). command: `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy evt-ingest-key --project=redwood-prod > /tmp/evt-policy.json` and `gsutil cp /tmp/evt-policy.json gs://redwood-audit/kms-snapshots/2629998888.json`

samuel: verified which workloads call the key: `kubectl -n telemetry get pods -o yaml | grep -E "evt-ingest-key|EVT_KEY_ID"` found 3 pods in canary and 12 in telemetry-prod. we'll need a rolling update.

ashley: escalated to incident process given cross-account principal. creating INC ticket and tagging legal/compliance. devops-bot: please create ticket. :rotating_light:

devops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-042. severity: P2. assignees: @ashley, @liam, @samuel. Slack thread pinned to the incident.

rachel: compliance note: partner contract clause 7.4 forbids persistent key-sharing without SC-delegation. we should flag for contract review.

ashley: short-term mitigation plan: 1) set `disable_time` on key, 2) deploy temp key in telemetry-canary, 3) run canary for 30m, 4) if ok, roll to prod in 15-min batches, 5) once stable remove external binding and rotate. I'll start step 1 at 09:00 UTC unless objections.

liam: +1. I'll coordinate the rolling restart windows with SRE — will open a restart-change and post ETA.

samuel: also recommend adding an automated lint: deny cross-account principals in KMS IAM via policy guardrails. we can add a check in the deploy pipeline: `if iam_member.endsWith("@partner-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com") fail`

ashley: agree — add as follow-up task. auditors: @auditor-bot, attaching the policy snapshot and last 7 days of KMS audit logs to the incident.

auditor-bot: attached artifacts: gs://redwood-audit/kms-snapshots/2629998888.json, gs://redwood-audit/kms-logs/2026-03-13_to_2026-03-20.json. Suggested tags: [kms, cross-account, entitlement-cleanup, incident].

rachel: thanks. once we wrap the rotation please prepare a short blameless postmortem summarizing root cause (how binding was added) and preventive controls (lint, periodic RBAC sampling).

ashley: will do. starting step 1 now and will post updates here. :lock:

liam: update 09:07 UTC — disabled key flagged, canary scheduled at 09:20. posting change link: https://deployments.internal/change/CHG-8891

samuel: tracking: removed external binding in a dry-run on a staging copy. verified no failing decrypts after switching the canary pods to temp key.

ashley: 09:45 UTC — canary looks green (30m). starting the rolling update for telemetry-prod. ETA ~40m. will keep thread updated. :white_check_mark:
